slides.texte_overlay:
5 posture mistakes that kill
your charisma in public
Mistake 1: rounded shoulders. Hours over a laptop pull them forward, and it makes you look tired and unsure. Roll them back and down, like you're putting them in your back pockets. Instant change.
Mistake 2: looking at the floor while walking. Eyes down reads as "don't notice me." Look ahead, at eye level, as if you're looking for a friend across the street. People start making way for you.
Mistake 3: hands in your pockets all night. It hides your hands and closes you off. Keep one hand free, hold a drink, or let them rest naturally. Visible hands look calm and open.
Mistake 4: crossing your arms when you listen. Even if you're just cold, it reads as defensive. Keep your arms loose and your chest open, and people will feel far more comfortable around you.
Mistake 5: fidgeting. Tapping, playing with your phone, touching your face. Every small movement leaks nerves. Pick one still position and hold it. Stillness is the cheapest form of charisma.
Fix the inside too. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives you real things to say. Good posture gets people's attention. A sharp, curious mind is what keeps it.
slides.texte_sophia: I fixed my posture, then I started doing five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Good posture gets attention. A sharp mind keeps it.

slides.texte_overlay: The fix: two minutes every morning. Back against a wall, head, shoulders and heels touching, breathe slowly. Do it for a month and standing tall stops being an effort. It just becomes you.
